LIVING THE CHARGE
Talent is everywhere.
Opportunity is not.

We are fundraising $100,000 to give talented high school students access to internships and volunteer opportunities without cost becoming a barrier.

Donate
SEE OUR IMPACT
WHAT WE DO
Bridging the gap between
talent and opportunity.

Living the Charge is a US-registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit working to bridge the gap between talent and opportunity. We believe every talented Kenyan student deserves the chance to pursue experiences that can shape their future, regardless of their financial circumstances.

Through our $100,000 endowment, we seek to support 250 high school students annually in pursuing meaningful internships and volunteer opportunities turning potential into possibility and opportunity into lasting impact.

Cost should never be a barrier to opportunity.
KENYA / 2026
$100K+
ENDOWMENT TARGET

BUILD THE FUND

Contributions grow the permanent endowment.

02
GENERATE RETURNS

Long-term investment supports 250 students annually.

03
FUND OPPORTUNITIES

Proceeds cater for food, transport and liability insurance expenses.

WHY WE DO THIS
To whom much is given, much is required.

We are beneficiaries of the goodwill of those who invested in us before they knew what we would become.

Living the Charge exists to close the gap between brilliance and access, creating an avenue for us to give others the opportunity we once needed ourselves.

Learn more about our mission
The people Living the Charge
The power of your donation.

Imagine having all the talent in the world but no avenue to express it! That is the reality that we grew up in while we were in Kenya, and we seek to make a difference for those that come after us.

Every contribution creates generational and sustainable impact that truly lasts a lifetime.

Read the full stories of our students

LIVING THE CHARGE
Our mission

To bridge the gap between talent and opportunity by making meaningful professional experiences accessible to talented Kenyan students, regardless of their financial circumstances.

WHAT WE BELIEVE

Talent should never be limited by the cost of opportunity.

We believe every promising student deserves the chance to gain experience, build connections, and discover their potential.

Living The Charge helps remove the everyday financial barriers such as transport, meals, and other participation costs that can keep students from accessing these opportunities.

OUR POINT OF DEPARTURE

Rooted in Starehe.
Built for Africa.

Living the Charge builds on Starehe Boys’ Centre’s Voluntary Service Scheme, a programme that has connected students with service and professional exposure since 1976.

The model has historically depended on informal pledges and temporary funding. When resources fall short, students can lose access simply because basic participation costs cannot be covered.

1976
Starehe VSS begins

A tradition of structured service and professional exposure takes root.

Today
Build permanent funding

Living the Charge turns that tradition into durable financial infrastructure.

Kenya
Expand across schools

More talented students gain access without cost becoming a barrier.

Africa
Build a wider network

A long-term opportunity network connects students, schools, and employers.

LEADERSHIP

Built by people who understand the opportunity gap firsthand.
Socrates Okong'o

FOUNDER

University of Pennsylvania undergraduate and Starehe Boys' Centre alumnus.

Ricky Ouko

CO-FOUNDER

Georgia State University undergraduate and Starehe Boys' Centre alumnus.

MENTOR A STUDENT

Moving beyond donations
How You Can Help

We All Have Something to Offer. Here's how you can Live the Charge.

Career Guidance

Share your journey, career advice, university guidance, and lessons you wish you had known.

Practical Exposure

Offer job shadowing, workplace exposure, or insight into what your profession looks like.

Skills & Workshops

Teach something you know well: coding, public speaking, finance, research, design, or another practical skill.

Connections & Mentorship

Be a role model, answer questions, or introduce a student to someone who can help them move forward.

WHO CAN MENTOR?

We all have something to offer

If your experience could help a young person find direction, you have something valuable to share.

Lawyers, engineers, doctors, entrepreneurs, artists, researchers, tradespeople, athletes, and professionals from every background are welcome.

“

A mentor is someone who sees more talent and ability within you, than you see in yourself, and helps bring it out of you.

— BOB PROCTOR

Simple, flexible, and built around your availability.

01

02

We connect you with a student whose interests align with your experience.

03

Connect virtually or in person. You decide how much time you can give and how you would like to help.
